- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/24 (Wed) 17:15
- [USER] User inquired about the safety of exercising with asthma.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is safe to exercise if you have asthma; regular exercise can strengthen respiratory muscles and improve lung capacity.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Precautions may be necessary to avoid asthma symptoms during exercise.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended using an inhaler before exercising to prevent asthma symptoms.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested warming up properly before exercising to avoid asthma symptoms.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised choosing a sport suitable for the user's fitness level that does not require extreme effort.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Encouraged listening to the body and taking breaks if asthma symptoms occur during exercise.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended seeking immediate medical attention if asthma symptoms do not subside after taking a break.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested consulting a doctor before starting to exercise with asthma for personalized advice.
- [USER] User asked for advice on improving their flexion technique in skiing.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended practicing proper posture while skiing, keeping shoulders back and trunk upright.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised that flexion should occur mainly at the hips and knees, not the back.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested practicing dynamic flexion on flat terrain and gentle slopes to improve control and balance.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended practicing static flexion on flat terrain and gentle slopes to enhance control and balance.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Encouraged practicing flexion in various snow conditions and on different types of slopes to build skill and confidence.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested taking ski lessons with a certified instructor if the user struggles to improve their flexion technique independently.
